caseStudyHeader.heading: Javelin Program
caseStudyHeader.body: A 12-week design thinking coaching program for IBM's top 80 client account teams.

summary.label: Goal
summary.description: The coaching program needed to contextualize design thinking for consultants to differentiate them throughout the sales cycle.

summary.label: Outcomes
summary.description: The program influenced 1.2B in revenue and trail blazed design thinking in the sales context and remains a template for similar efforts.

summary.label: Role
summary.description: I was a service designer, facilitator, and coach working with a small design team. My biggest contribution to the project developing learning objectives, habits, and onboarding sales teams.

summary.label: Client and scope
summary.description: The internal client was the IBM Global Markets SVP of Integrated Accounts and my role on this team lasted just under 2 years between 2017 and 2019.

pullout.statement: How might we design a better way for account sellers to differentiate IBM in the sales cycle?

list: IBM's adoption of design thinking reached across the company except sales, even as client engagements showed it could impact sales performance.
Changing markets pushed sellers toward new, design-led ways of working, leading the new Enterprise Design Thinking for Sellers team to form the Javelin Program.
To teach sellers design thinking, the program's format had to fit how they actually worked.
Our vision focused on four core seller jobs, enabled by Enterprise Design Thinking.
